llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its comic/script-writing purpose; it writes simple local logs but requests no credentials or network access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (comic storyboard, panels, dialogue) align with the included scripts: scripts/comic.sh produces storyboard, character, dialogue, and layout templates; scripts/script.sh provides content-drafting helpers (headlines, outlines, SEO) which are broadly consistent with content creation. No unrelated credentials or binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs running the CLI; it does not request system-wide data. The shipped scripts create a user data directory and append logs (history.log, data.log) under $DATA_DIR (defaults to ${COMIC_SCRIPT_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/comic-script}). Inputs given to many commands are recorded to these local logs. This is expected for a CLI but worth noting if you do not want your prompts persisted locally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads; this is an instruction-and-script bundle. No network-based install or extraction from external URLs is present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, no secrets or tokens. The scripts respect an optional COMIC_SCRIPT_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME/HOME fallback for locating the data directory — standard behavior for CLI tooling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and model invocation settings are default. The skill only writes to its own data folder under the user's home directory and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: generate comic/storyboard templates and provide content-writing helpers. It does create and append to logs in a data directory (by default ~/.local/share/comic-script), so avoid passing sensitive secrets or private content as command arguments if you don't want them recorded. There are no network calls or credential requests in the code, but SKILL.md links to bytesagain.com for feedback — that link is informational only (the scripts do not contact it). If you install, review or change the DATA_DIR location (set COMIC_SCRIPT_DIR) if you prefer logs somewhere else, and inspect the scripts yourself before running to confirm behavior matches your expectations.
